newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares rise on dollar, more gains up front.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares rise on dollar, more gains up front.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher again on Tuesday, fuelled by the strong dollar with more advances expected by dealers depending on Wall Street's overnight performance.
"If the U.S. market performs reasonably well, we should see more gains tomorrow," one dealer said but the Dow Jones slipped and American bond yields rose in early Wall Street trading.
The KFX top-20 index finished 1.33 point or 0.88 percent up at 152.43, while the KFX June future rose 1.85 point to 152.25 with 60 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Dollar-sensitive Danish stock did generally well. Superfos climbed 25 crowns to finish at 760, FLS hit its highest point of the year, rising 12 crowns to a closing 885. Novo Nordisk advanced 16 crowns to 670 and Radiometer put on 16 crowns to end at 390, while Moeller's D/S Svendborg and D/S 1912, which normally react positively to a firmer dollar, were little moved, hit possibly by ongoing low oil prices.
Overall turnover for the day was 898 million crowns. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33-969652
